site.address: Madla Gate, Madla, Panna, Madhya Pradesh, India

pwt_destination.title: Madla Gate — Panna Core Zone
pwt_destination.excerpt: Primary core-zone gate with the most safari routes and the thickest lodge belt nearby.
pwt_destination.content: Panna's main entry to the core zone, ideal for first-time visitors and most itineraries. Routes run through teak and dry deciduous forest, rocky ridges and Ken river gorges. Highest demand — book 30-60 days ahead.

pwt_destination.title: Hinouta Gate — Panna Core Zone
pwt_destination.excerpt: Core-zone gate on the Panna-Khajuraho road, ideal for travellers arriving from Khajuraho.
pwt_destination.content: Core entry from the Khajuraho highway (~35 km from the temples). Less saturated than Madla on many days and a natural fit for a Panna + Khajuraho loop.

pwt_destination.title: Akola Gate — Panna Buffer Zone
pwt_destination.excerpt: Buffer-side eco-tourism gate with seasonal, permit-based availability.
pwt_destination.content: Used for eco-tourism and some community routes. Quieter and often more affordable when open. Availability is seasonal — we confirm current status before quoting.

pwt_destination.title: Pandav Caves & Falls
pwt_destination.excerpt: Fascinating caves and waterfall surrounded by natural scenery and local legends.
pwt_destination.content: Explore the Pandav Caves and Waterfall, where a 30-metre cascade falls into a famously heart-shaped pool. A short, rewarding trail leads through rock and woodland to the caves and waterfall — one of the most photogenic spots in the Panna region. Best after light monsoon rain; suitable for families.

pwt_destination.title: Raneh Waterfall
pwt_destination.excerpt: Dramatic natural beauty where the Ken River flows through a spectacular rocky canyon.
pwt_destination.content: The Ken drops through layered volcanic rock — granite, sandstone and crimson rhyolite — creating a narrow gorge with several waterfalls, especially after monsoon. Half-day trip from Panna town; ideal for photographers. Best August to February for full flow.

pwt_destination.title: Khajuraho Western Temples
pwt_destination.excerpt: Magnificent Western Group of Temples renowned for remarkable architecture and intricate stone carvings.
pwt_destination.content: A UNESCO World Heritage site, Khajuraho's Western Group preserves Chandela-era temples famous for their shikhara towers and dense, expressive stone carving. About 35 km from Panna. Morning or evening light transforms the sandstone into gold.

pwt_destination.title: Ken Gharial Sanctuary
pwt_destination.excerpt: River sanctuary where ancient gharials bask — a rare wildlife spectacle on the Ken.
pwt_destination.content: On the banks of the Ken, a stretch of river protects one of India's ancient crocodilians — the gharial. See them basking on sandbars, and hear the story of their return from the brink. Mugger crocodiles share the same sandbars. Best November to March, morning or late afternoon.

pwt_destination.title: Panna Temples
pwt_destination.excerpt: Discover the spiritual side of Panna through its historic and culturally significant temples.
pwt_destination.content: From the streets of Panna town to nearby villages, the district is dotted with living temples that anchor local festivals, folk song and traditional music. Baldau Mandir and Jugalkishor Mandir are the best-known landmarks — quiet, atmospheric and easy to visit between safaris.

pwt_destination.title: Kutni Dam
pwt_destination.excerpt: A peaceful escape surrounded by water and natural landscapes — perfect for relaxing and enjoying the scenery.
pwt_destination.content: Kutni Dam is a calm reservoir on the edge of the district — a half-day escape for slow travellers who want sky, water and stillness. Great for a relaxed picnic, quiet birding and sunset photography.

pwt_destination.title: Walk with Pardhi
pwt_destination.excerpt: Experience nature on foot and learn more about the local environment and traditional knowledge.
pwt_destination.content: The Pardhi community has read this landscape for generations. On a guided walk you will see the forest through their eyes — tracking signs, edible and medicinal plants, and the rhythms of village life around Panna. Gentle walk, local guides, early morning or late afternoon departures.

pwt_destination.title: Ken Riverside Scenes
pwt_destination.excerpt: Peaceful riverside locations, breathtaking views and memorable sunsets along the Ken River.
pwt_destination.content: The Ken cuts a calm, dramatic line through the reserve. Selected riverside points offer the best of it — basking gharials, cliff-nesting vultures, kingfishers over still water and sunsets that turn the sandstone gold. Winter is a birding hotspot for photographers.

pwt_destination.title: Bird Watching
pwt_destination.excerpt: Panna is a birder's haven — over 200 species across teak forest, grassland and the Ken river.
pwt_destination.content: From red-headed vultures on the Ken cliffs to crested serpent eagles over the plateau, pied kingfishers and lapwings on the river — our guides know the calls, roosts and seasonal migrants. Best November to March. Binoculars and field guide provided on guided trips.

pwt_safari.title: Morning Jeep Safari — Madla Gate
pwt_safari.excerpt: Morning core-zone safari with naturalist support and priority wildlife routes.
pwt_safari.content: Enter via Madla Gate at the first light of the day. Fresh tracks, active movement and cooler air. Reporting is 30-45 minutes before gate opening (summer 05:30 / winter 06:30).

pwt_safari.title: Evening Jeep Safari — Madla Gate
pwt_safari.excerpt: Evening slot with golden light and leisurely pace.
pwt_safari.content: Afternoon core-zone drive (summer 15:30 / winter 14:30). Warm light, relaxed pace, great for families and photographers.

pwt_safari.title: Hinouta Gate Safari — Khajuraho Route
pwt_safari.excerpt: Core-zone safari entered from the Panna-Khajuraho highway.
pwt_safari.content: Ideal when combining Panna with Khajuraho (~35 km). Less saturated on many days with its own route variety.

pwt_safari.title: Ken River Boat Safari (Seasonal)
pwt_safari.excerpt: Guide-led boat ride past gharials, gorges and nesting vulture cliffs.
pwt_safari.content: Seasonal, water-level dependent. We confirm current forest-department permission and availability before booking.

pwt_safari.title: Jungle Safari (Buffer) — Akola
pwt_safari.excerpt: Quieter buffer-zone safari with leopard, deer and rare bird sightings.
pwt_safari.content: Buffer-zone routes around Akola blend riverine habitat and open scrub — strong for leopards, sambar, chital and a long list of birds. Evening and seasonal night drives available where the forest department permits.

pwt_package.subtitle: Weekend tiger trail
pwt_package.excerpt: All-inclusive weekend break: two safaris, one night in a gate-side lodge, transfers and coordination.
pwt_package.content: Day 1 arrival + evening safari; Day 2 morning safari + checkout. One quote covering permits, gypsy, guide, stay (AP) and lodge-gate transfers.

pwt_resort.title: Ken Vihar Jungle Lodge
pwt_resort.excerpt: Premium gate-side lodge with full restaurant and pickup support.
pwt_resort.content: Spacious cottages and tented suites, lawns, full restaurant, hot water round the clock. 3 km from Madla gate with pickup/drop.

pwt_resort.title: Panna Gate View Cottages
pwt_resort.excerpt: Clean budget cottages 2 km from Madla gate with basic meals.
pwt_resort.content: Simple rooms, attached bath, in-house basic meals. 2 km from Madla gate; early-morning departure handled. Best for budget travellers.

pwt_resort.title: Tiger Den Luxury Resort
pwt_resort.excerpt: Luxury resort with pool, spa-style service and curated dining.
pwt_resort.content: Pool, premium rooms, curated dining and guided stays. 9 km from Madla gate with private transfers. Best for honeymoons and premium wildlife weeks.

pwt_resort.title: Hinouta Riverside Stay
pwt_resort.excerpt: Premium stay on the Khajuraho road, 1 km from Hinouta gate.
pwt_resort.content: Ideal for the last night of a Panna + Khajuraho loop. Riverside setting, full meals, pickup/drop.

pwt_vehicle.title: Open Gypsy 6-Seater — Safari Fleet
pwt_vehicle.excerpt: Official safari-compatible open vehicle with trained driver support.
pwt_vehicle.content: Primary vehicle for core and buffer wildlife drives. Best for small groups and photographers requiring open-angle visibility.

pwt_vehicle.title: Canter 20-Seater — Group Safari
pwt_vehicle.excerpt: Zone-approved canter for larger groups on limited routes.
pwt_vehicle.content: For big groups and budget travellers. Route availability is zone-approved and limited — confirm at booking.

pwt_faq.title: What is the best time to visit Panna Tiger Reserve?
pwt_faq.content: The best period for wildlife sightings is October to June, with the finest combination of weather and activity from February to April. The reserve closes for the core monsoon season each year.

pwt_faq.title: How many people can sit in a Panna safari gypsy?
pwt_faq.content: The open 4x4 gypsy seats up to 6 people including driver and guide. We recommend 4-5 guests for comfortable photography positions.

pwt_faq.title: Which ID do I need for the safari permit?
pwt_faq.content: One valid government photo ID per visitor (Aadhaar, PAN, Passport or Voter ID). Names must match the ID exactly.

pwt_faq.title: Do I need to book Panna safari in advance?
pwt_faq.content: Yes, strongly. Core-zone permits for Madla and Hinouta open online about 60 days ahead and peak-season weekend slots sell out fast. 30-60 days' lead time is ideal.

pwt_faq.title: Are entry fees included in the safari price?
pwt_faq.content: Official forest charges are billed at the actual rate on your permit. Our quotes itemise them separately so you always see what you are paying for.

pwt_faq.title: Is a tiger sighting guaranteed?
pwt_faq.content: No. Sightings are natural events. Good slot and zone planning improves your chances — we plan routes with that in mind.

pwt_faq.title: Is the Ken River boat safari available all year?
pwt_faq.content: No. It runs seasonally when the forest department permits boating and water levels allow, typically winter through early summer. We confirm current status before booking.

pwt_faq.title: Is there a night safari inside Panna core zone?
pwt_faq.content: Night drives are not part of regular core-zone permits. Where the forest department permits buffer-zone drives we arrange them; otherwise we are transparent about it.

pwt_faq.title: Which gate should I choose for my first Panna safari?
pwt_faq.content: Madla. It is the primary core-zone gate with the most routes and the thickest lodge belt nearby.

pwt_faq.title: Which is the best area to stay for Panna safari?
pwt_faq.content: The Madla gate belt (2-10 km). It is the primary core-zone gate, so you avoid long pre-safari drives.

pwt_faq.title: Do package prices change?
pwt_faq.content: Prices are indicative. Forest fees and seasonal stay rates can move; we reconfirm the exact figure before you pay.

pwt_faq.title: Can I customise a package?
pwt_faq.content: Yes, most travellers do — swap lodges, add Khajuraho, add a boat ride. We rebuild the quote line-by-line.
